reversal_steps: Active sessions are terminated permanently
Users must re-authenticate to create new sessions
reversal_basis: Session revocation forces all active tokens to expire immediately. Re-authentication creates brand new sessions. This is intentional isolation behavior per NIST SP 800-61r2 containment guidance.
source_reference: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.3.1 Containment — https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-61r2.pdf | OWASP: Session revocation — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html
risk_if_not_reversed: All legitimate users temporarily logged out — resolved on re-auth within minutes

reversal_steps: Generate a replacement API key via the respective service
Update all dependent integrations with the new key
reversal_basis: API keys are single-use secrets — once revoked they cannot be restored. Best practice per NIST SP 800-63B is immediate revocation of compromised credentials, followed by issuing a new key.
risk_if_not_reversed: All services using the revoked API key receive 401/403 errors until updated

reversal_steps: Generate a new certificate signing request (CSR)
Submit to CA for signing
Deploy new certificate to affected services
reversal_basis: Digital certificate revocation is permanent (CRL/OCSP). Per RFC 5280, revoked certificates remain in the CRL indefinitely. A new certificate with a new serial number must be issued.
source_reference: RFC 5280 §3.3 — https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280 | NIST SP 800-57 Key Management — https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/sp/800-57-part-1/rev-5/final
risk_if_not_reversed: TLS/mTLS connections using the revoked certificate are rejected

reversal_steps: User must re-enroll TOTP/FIDO2 device through account security portal
Admin may need to initiate MFA reset
reversal_basis: MFA device (TOTP, FIDO2) deregistration is reversible by re-enrollment. Per NIST SP 800-63B, re-enrollment must use identity proofing. A new device is enrolled, not the old one restored.
risk_if_not_reversed: User cannot complete MFA challenge and is locked out until re-enrolled

reversal_steps: Remove the 'must change password at next logon' flag via IAM/AD admin portal
reversal_basis: Password change requirements are flags on user accounts (e.g., AD pwdLastSet=0 or IAM 'PasswordResetRequired'). These flags can be cleared by an admin if the requirement was set in error. Reversing needs security team approval.
source_reference: Microsoft AD: pwdLastSet attribute — https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/adschema/a-pwdlastset | AWS IAM: update-login-profile — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/iam/update-login-profile.html
risk_if_not_reversed: User must change password on next login (minor operational friction)

reversal_steps: Remove step-up authentication policy or session extension grant
reversal_basis: Step-up MFA requirements are policy configurations on the IdP/application session. Removing the policy reverts to standard session lifetime. Short-lived security measure by design.
risk_if_not_reversed: Users repeatedly prompted for MFA (operational friction)

reversal_steps: Revert to standing access by disabling JIT policy in PAM tool (CyberArk, BeyondTrust, AWS IAM Identity Center)
reversal_basis: JIT access is implemented via PAM tools that require approval workflows for sensitive access. Reverting to standing access requires disabling the JIT policy and approving restoration. Per CIS Controls 6.5 principle of least privilege.
source_reference: CIS Controls v8 Control 6 — https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/v8/ | CyberArk JIT — https://docs.cyberark.com/Product-Doc/OnlineHelp/PAS/Latest/en/Content/PASIMP/jit-access.htm
risk_if_not_reversed: Administrative access requires per-request approval (operational slowdown)

reversal_steps: Re-enable account via IAM/AD console
AWS: aws iam update-login-profile / update-access-key --status Active
AD: Enable-ADAccount -Identity <user>
reversal_basis: Account suspension preserves all account attributes while blocking access. Re-enabling is a single administrative action. Per NIST SP 800-61r2, account suspension is a standard containment action during incident investigation.

reversal_steps: Re-enable service account credentials in the relevant platform
Azure: Enable Service Principal. GCP: enable SA. K8s: restore ServiceAccount
reversal_basis: Service account revocation disables the service identity. All services running under it fail authentication. Re-enabling the account and distributing new credentials restores operation.
risk_if_not_reversed: All services running as this SA lose authentication access

reversal_steps: Re-assign the role to the user/group via IAM, AD, or application RBAC console
reversal_basis: Role assignment in RBAC systems is additive/removable. Revoking a role removes permissions granted by that role. Re-assigning it restores them. Per AC-6 (Least Privilege), a re-assignment should be re-justified.
risk_if_not_reversed: User loses all permissions granted by the revoked role

reversal_steps: Re-grant data access through DBAC/DAC policy
Update SaaS platform sharing settings or IAM data policies
reversal_basis: Data access controls (SharePoint permissions, Google Drive ACLs, database role grants) are configurable. Revoking removes access entries. Re-granting restores them. Business justification required for reversal.
risk_if_not_reversed: Users/services cannot access required data resources

reversal_steps: MySQL/Postgres: GRANT <privs> ON <db>.* TO '<user>'@'<host>';
MSSQL: GRANT <permission> ON <object> TO <principal>;
reversal_basis: SQL GRANT/REVOKE are standard DML commands. REVOKE removes a privilege; GRANT restores it. Original grant details must be known (what was revoked).
risk_if_not_reversed: Application/user cannot perform previously authorized database operations

reversal_steps: Generate replacement token in the third-party integration settings
Update integration configuration with new token
reversal_basis: Integration tokens (Slack, GitHub, Jira, etc.) are single-use secrets. Once revoked, they cannot be restored. New tokens must be generated and distributed to dependent systems.
source_reference: GitHub: Revoking tokens — https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/reviewing-your-authorized-oauth-apps | OWASP API Security Top 10
risk_if_not_reversed: Third-party integration broken until new token is configured

reversal_steps: JWTs are self-contained and cannot be un-revoked
User must log in again to receive a new JWT
reversal_basis: JWTs are stateless by design (RFC 7519). Revocation requires server-side token blocklisting. The specific token cannot be 'un-revoked'; the user obtains a new token on re-authentication.
source_reference: RFC 7519 JWT — https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7519 | OWASP: JWT Security — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/JSON_Web_Token_for_Java_Cheat_Sheet.html
risk_if_not_reversed: User is logged out from all sessions — resolved on re-authentication

reversal_steps: SAML assertions are one-time use (NotOnOrAfter constraint)
User must re-authenticate through IdP to receive a new assertion
reversal_basis: SAML 2.0 assertions are short-lived (typically 5 minutes) per the spec. Revoking forces early expiry. New assertions are generated on IdP re-authentication.
risk_if_not_reversed: User is logged out from SP — resolved on next IdP authentication

reversal_steps: Application must re-authenticate via OAuth2 client credentials flow to get a new token
reversal_basis: OAuth2 application tokens (client credentials flow) cannot be un-revoked. The application re-authenticates with client_id/client_secret to get a new access token.
source_reference: RFC 6749 OAuth2 §4.4 — https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749 | RFC 7009 Token Revocation — https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7009
risk_if_not_reversed: Application API calls fail — resolved when application re-authenticates

reversal_steps: Generate a new share link in the sharing application (Google Drive, SharePoint, OneDrive)
reversal_basis: Share link revocation invalidates the specific URL token. A new share link can be generated with the same permissions. The new link gets a different URL token.
source_reference: Google Drive: Sharing files — https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2494822 | Microsoft SharePoint: Sharing links — https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/share-sharepoint-files-or-folders
risk_if_not_reversed: External recipients with the revoked link lose access
